text:
marta: quick check-in after the transport deep-dive: websocket multiplexing for realtime inferencing is live in canary, and it exposes a thorny question: how do we guarantee billing_key propagation across multiplexed streams when sampling/shedder/route decisions happen at different layers?

jules: short summary of the problem i saw: a single ws conn can carry N logical requests from different tenants. we either (A) attach per-message headers (subprotocol/meta) or (B) rely on a per-connection envelope that maps substreams -> attrs. both interact poorly with our sampling layer which currently samples at the connection ingress.

kai: exactly. if sampling is conn-level and we drop a connection, we lose multiple tenants' telemetry in one shot which biases cost attribution and SLOs. Conn-level sampling is cheaper but gives us coarse visibility.

marta: we need billing accuracy for chargeback and to trigger quota enforcement early. losing whole-conn attribution is risky. what's the perf delta if we move to per-message tagging?

rachel: did a microbenchmark: per-message attrs == ~0.5% extra CPU on proxy under current traffic and an extra ~55 bytes/msg (JSON submeta). connection-level attr reduces bytes but increases worst-case attribution loss.

jules: also note protocol concerns: some clients use binary frames where inserting JSON submeta requires a framing wrapper. That implies SDK changes. mobile/web will need updates.

kai: another angle: could we keep conn-level header but emit a periodic "heartbeat map" that lists active substreams with their billing_keys and short TTLs. proxies can consume the map for routing/sampling and accept per-message light ids that reference map entries. this reduces payload per msg but requires map state.

marta: love the map idea. tradeoffs: stateful proxies (complexity), TTL expiry semantics, and reconciling map on reconnects. Also map leaks state if client disconnects uncleanly.

rachel: map approach perf: heartbeats every 5s added ~0.1% CPU and 2000 req/s per proxy for a 50k conn fleet. Seems acceptable but increases memory footprint per-proxy by ~6KB/conn for maps.

jules: operational burden: when proxies crash we need fast resync. Also how do we instrument map misses for alerting? we should expose metric `ws.attr.map.miss` and `ws.attr.ref.fallback` (ref meaning per-message ref missing -> full unwrap).

kai: for sampling we can introduce hybrid sampling: prefer per-message sampling decision at ingress if message contains explicit billing_ref; otherwise fallback to conn-sample with probabilistic per-stream demuxing. That reduces blast radius.

marta: decision criteria time: must satisfy (a) billing key present at first router for >99% of requests in canary, (b) increase in proxy CPU <2% in canary, (c) SDK changes minimal for web clients.

rachel: with heartbeats + per-message refs we can hit those targets in canary numbers i measured: billing_present ~99.3%, CPU +0.8% for current canary.

jules: rollout plan suggestion: 1) implement heartbeat map and lightweight per-message ref (2 bytes id) in proxy + server; 2) SDK patch for web to send heartbeat for multiplexed flows (opt-in); 3) telemetry: add metrics `ws.attr.presence` (present|ref|none), `ws.attr.map.miss`, and `ws.attr.source` (conn|heartbeat|permsg); 4) canary with subset of customers who opt-in to web SDK bump.

kai: for backwards compatibility: if client doesn't signal multiplexing, treat connection as single-tenant and continue conn-level attribution. Also default TTL for map entries = 12s to bound staleness.

marta: security/privacy note: heartbeat maps must *not* include tenant PII. only opaque ids and short lived refs. add enforcement in proxy to reject any heartbeat containing raw emails/uuids that look PII-like.

rachel: I'll add a linter rule and a small sanitizer in the proxy. Will also record the perf numbers and memory impact in the spike doc.

jules: i'll draft the short RFC addendum with message framing examples (text and binary) and reference code snippets for the web SDK. Need to call out the cost-accounting guarantees and fallback semantics.

kai: one more: queues and async fanout currently assume per-request envelope. when we demux refs we must ensure that the async path preserves the ref to rehydrate billing_key for post-processing. that's on eng-platform + ingest-team to align.

marta: agree. add ingest-team to owners in the RFC. owners: jules (protocol + RFC), rachel (proxy perf + sanitizer), kai (sampling semantics), sam (ingest alignment, added offline), marta (product + rollout).

ingest-bot: telemetry snapshot: ws_canary: conn_count=48k, billing_attr_present=0.993, avg_proxy_cpu_inc=0.8%, ws_attr_map_miss=0.0012

marta: great numbers. plan: proceed with heartbeat-map prototype and small SDK opt-in. reconvene Tues 9am to review spike and draft RFC. If map_miss climbs >0.5% during canary rollback to per-message full envelope for that client. :thumbsup:
